questions.explanation: In a typical dicot leaf epidermis, guard cells contain chloroplasts whereas ordinary epidermal pavement cells usually do not. Guard cells also possess nuclei and vacuoles. Their changes in turgor regulate the opening of the stomatal pore.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: In botanical growth-form terminology, herbs differ from shrubs because herbs
questions.explanation: In botanical usage, herbs are herbaceous plants with nonwoody above-ground stems. Shrubs retain woody stems. Herbs can be annual, biennial or perennial, and the word does not mean that the plant must be medicinal.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: A hydrogen-to-oxygen atomic ratio of 2:1 is commonly associated with which class of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Many common carbohydrates have hydrogen and oxygen atoms in a 2:1 ratio, as in glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆. This ratio is a useful introductory clue, but it does not alone prove that an unknown compound is a carbohydrate; there are exceptions and other compounds with the same ratio.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which pair is especially associated with chlorophyll formation, one element being its central metal atom and the other being required for its synthesis?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is the central metal atom in chlorophyll. Iron is required for processes involved in chlorophyll synthesis, although it is not the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule. Deficiency of either can therefore impair normal green pigmentation.

questions.question: Movement of a plant part whose direction is independent of the direction of an external stimulus is called
questions.explanation: A nastic movement is a plant-part response whose direction is independent of the direction from which the stimulus arrives. In a tropism, the direction of growth depends on the stimulus direction. Phototropism concerns light, and thigmotropism concerns directional touch.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which listed part of the mammalian brain plays a major role in coordinating balance and posture?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum integrates sensory feedback and helps coordinate posture, balance and precise movements. It compares intended movement with incoming information and contributes corrective signals. Other brain regions also participate, but the cerebellum is the best answer here.

questions.question: What type of fruit is formed from a single flower having several free carpels?
questions.explanation: An aggregate fruit develops from several separate carpels of a single flower. Each carpel contributes a fruitlet. A multiple fruit instead develops from flowers grouped in an inflorescence, while a simple fruit comes from one ovary.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Maize rust is caused by fungi, such as Puccinia sorghi in common rust. The other listed diseases are viral: rinderpest, Newcastle disease, swine fever and cassava mosaic disease. A fungal rust pathogen is biologically different from a virus.

questions.question: An organism with two identical alleles at a particular gene locus is called
questions.explanation: An organism with two identical alleles at a particular gene locus is homozygous at that locus. For example, AA and aa are homozygous genotypes, whereas Aa is heterozygous. Diploid describes chromosome-set number rather than whether the two alleles match.

questions.question: The permanent dental formula 2 × (I 3/3, C 1/1, PM 4/4, M 2/3) gives 42 teeth. Which animal has this formula?
questions.explanation: An adult dog has, on each side, three upper and three lower incisors, one canine in each jaw, four premolars in each jaw, two upper molars and three lower molars. Doubling the one-side total gives 2 × (3 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 3) = 42 teeth.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Which statement about insectivorous plants is NOT true?

options.A: They obtain some nutrients by trapping and digesting insects
options.B: They attract insects only for pollination
options.C: They can grow in soils poor in nitrogenous nutrients
options.D: They supplement their nitrogen supply by digesting insects
options.E: Examples include butterworts, sundews and pitcher plants

questions.explanation: Insectivorous plants attract some insects as prey, not solely as pollinators. Digestion of prey supplies nutrients such as nitrogen, helping these plants live in nutrient-poor habitats. They generally still use photosynthesis to make carbohydrates.

questions.question: Starting just below the skull, which order correctly lists the vertebrae through the lumbar region?

options.A: Axis, atlas, remaining cervical, thoracic, lumbar

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: Positive phototropic bending of a coleoptile is brought about by

options.A: Auxin moving away from the region that elongates more
options.B: An even auxin distribution across both sides
options.C: Auxin inhibiting growth on the side that elongates more
options.D: Auxin accumulating on the shaded side and promoting greater elongation there
options.E: The absence of auxin in the coleoptile

questions.explanation: Under one-sided illumination, auxin becomes more concentrated on the shaded side of a coleoptile. At growth-promoting concentrations, cells there elongate more than cells on the illuminated side. The unequal elongation bends the shoot towards the light.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The swollen storage root of cassava is not a stem tuber because it

options.B: Has an aerial shoot elsewhere on the plant
options.C: Has other roots associated with it
options.E: Has an outer covering over its stored food

questions.explanation: Cassava’s swollen storage organ is a storage root. It lacks the axillary buds associated with nodes on a stem tuber. Storing food alone does not make an organ a stem: roots and modified stems can both act as food stores.

questions.subject: biology
questions.question: The main function of the middle-ear ossicles—malleus, incus and stapes—is
questions.explanation: The malleus, incus and stapes form a chain that transmits vibrations from the eardrum to the oval window of the inner ear. This transfer helps sound energy enter the fluid-filled inner ear. Balance is mainly sensed by the vestibular apparatus, not the ossicles.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to assess water clarity by measuring the depth at which it disappears from view?
questions.explanation: A Secchi disc is lowered into water to measure the depth at which it disappears from view, providing a measure of water transparency. Cloudier water usually reduces this depth. The reading is a clarity indicator, not a direct laboratory turbidity reading in NTU.
